Here, the first factor is $4\times 1$ matrix and the second factor is a $1\times 3$ matrix. 

There is $1$ column in the first matrix and $1$ row in the second matrix, so the product is well defined:

$$
4\times \boxed{\text{1}}✓\boxed{\text{1}}\times 3=4\times 3
$$

Computing the product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}-4 \\ -3 \\ -3 \\ -6\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}-3 & -8 & 4\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}(-4)\cdot (-3) & (-4)\cdot (-8) & (-4)\cdot 4 \\ (-3)\cdot (-3) & (-3)\cdot (-8) & (-3)\cdot 4 \\ (-3)\cdot (-3) & (-3)\cdot (-8) & (-3)\cdot 4 \\ (-6)\cdot (-3) & (-6)\cdot (-8) & (-6)\cdot 4\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}12 & 32 & -16 \\ 9 & 24 & -12 \\ 9 & 24 & -12 \\ 18 & 48 & -24\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$
